title: [CRY-9] Cross-epoch unlinkability claims contradict the chain-following design (and ARCHITECTURE §
description: Review finding CRY-9: Cross-epoch unlinkability claims contradict the chain-following design (and ARCHITECTURE §5) (lens CRY). Location: spec/10-relays.md:518, spec/12-security.md:34, spec/12-security.md:40, spec/12-security.md:46, spec/05-messaging.md:133, spec/05-messaging.md:216. Fix: 05:203 says "The relay thereby follows the chain from token to token". ARCHITECTURE §5 item 6 lists "which access-key chains (§6.2) are registered under each agreement" as within the IO budget. Yet 10:518 says a relay "cannot correlate them without also capturing the epoch secrets", and 12:34 says it cannot "Map routing tables across epochs". Both are false. 05:216 claims the wrapper hides "epoch boundaries and which messages are Commits", but the routing envelope carries `epoch` in clear (05:186), and the announcement rides on the envelope carrying the Commit (05:203). 05:133 ("tokens of different key epochs are unlinkable") is false for broadcast because of 05:136. Rewrite as proposed: chains are linkable but not mappable to a channel or Space; epoch numbers and Commits are visible; the wrapper hides `group_id`, `content_type` and sender data. Remove or qualify the decoy rationale at 12:46. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
